relevance_note: The paper describes two affected twins first-hand: "These findings led to ALDH5A1 sequencing which revealed homozygous c.608C>T; pPro203Leu mutations, previously described as disease causing, in both subjects."
method_note: Built by hand-written Python (all values from my reading). In-scope: Twin A, Twin B (first-hand), their two parents and two siblings ("The parents were confirmed as heterozygous as were two siblings"; sex not stated, labelled parent/sibling of Twin A), three previously published affected siblings of the earlier Indian family (Gibson et al. 1997; facts: death at 13, diagnosis at 9 and 3 years; the two younger ones are labelled in the order the ages are printed), and one adult diagnosed at 62 (Lapalme-Remis et al. 2015; male per 'his family'). The 182 literature/database cases (Table 1) are counts by country only and get no rows. The Markdown prints '>' as '>'; spans keep '>', values use '>'. The Results print the protein as 'pPro203Leu' (no dot); the abstract prints 'p.Pro203Leu'; the twins' variant value uses the abstract form, the relatives' rows use the Results form. Twins' inheritance: both parents stated heterozygous, enum has no biallelic option, so 'inherited unspecified parent' was used. 'Levetiracetam was initiated recently when the breakthrough seizure occurred in the twin brother' (in Twin B's paragraph) is ambiguous about which twin received levetiracetam or had the breakthrough seizure, so it is left out of both. Abstract and Discussion statements about 'the probands'/'the twins' (global developmental delay, expressive aphasia, chorea as 'typical') were not used where the per-twin paragraphs differ (chorea is stated only for Twin A). Incoordination (Twin A) and impaired motor coordination (Twin B) were not mapped to the 'ataxia' checklist item. Twin B hyperactivity alone was not mapped to 'attention problems or ADHD'. MRI was done in Twin A only. 'No known ... family history of neurodevelopmental disorders' was not used to exclude features for relatives. Consanguinity 'no' is from 'no known history of consanguinity'. No contradictions found.
